Used $6$ m as the height of the right-hand part instead of $3$ m.

questions.solution_text:
Split the L into a tall left rectangle and a low right rectangle.
$A_1 = 3\times 6$
$= 18\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = 5\times 3$
$= 15\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 + A_2$

questions.question_text: A trapezium-shaped garden has parallel sides $14$ m and $8$ m, and the distance between them is $6$ m. Calculate its area.

options.why: Did not halve $(a+b)\times h$ in the trapezium formula.
Multiplied the two parallel sides and halved, ignoring the height.
Treated the shape as a triangle with base $14$ m and height $6$ m.
Found the area of the $8$ by $7$ bounding rectangle around the whole shape.
Used $7$ m for the stem's height instead of $5$ m.
Found only the top bar and left out the stem.

questions.solution_text:
Split the T into the top bar and the stem.
$A_1 = 8\times 2$
$= 16\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = 3\times 5$
$= 15\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 + A_2$
$= 31\text{ m}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
A lawn is shaped like a $10$ m by $6$ m rectangle with a triangle of height $4$ m on one end.
Turf is sold in rolls that each cover $9\text{ m}^{2}$, and rolls cannot be split.
How many rolls are needed?

options.why: Rounded the number of rolls down instead of up.
Did not halve the triangle, giving an area of $100\text{ m}^{2}$ before dividing.
Divided the area by $8\text{ m}^{2}$ per roll instead of $9\text{ m}^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
$A_1 = 10\times 6$
$= 60\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\times 10\times 4$
$= 20\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 + A_2$
$= 80\text{ m}^{2}$
$80\div 9 = 8.8\ldots$
Rolls cannot be split, so $9$ rolls are needed.
